Generate an OCSP responder certificate and sign it with the CA
output: openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout ocsp.key -out ocsp.csr -subj "/CN=ocsp.example.com" && openssl ca -config ca.conf -extensions ocsp -in ocsp.csr -out ocsp.crt -batch

instruction: Verify that a certificate is an OCSP responder certificate by checking extensions
output: openssl x509 -in ocsp.crt -text -noout | grep -A5 'Netscape Cert Type\|Extended Key Usage'

instruction: Create a PEM-encoded certificate chain file from individual certificates
Extract individual certificates from a combined PEM chain file
Check the OCSP responder certificate expiry and compare with the CA expiry
output: openssl x509 -in ocsp.crt -noout -enddate; openssl x509 -in ca.crt -noout -enddate

instruction: Display the authority key identifier and subject key identifier of a certificate
output: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout | grep -A2 'X509v3 Authority Key Identifier\|X509v3 Subject Key Identifier'

instruction: Generate a certificate with custom X.509 v3 extensions using a config file
output: openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout custom.key -out custom.csr -subj "/CN=custom.example.com" && openssl ca -config custom-ext.cnf -in custom.csr -out custom.crt -batch

instruction: Verify OCSP responder certificate is trusted by the CA for OCSP signing
output: openssl verify -CAfile ca.crt -purpose sslserver ocsp.crt; openssl ocsp -issuer ca.crt -cert ocsp.crt -text -url http://localhost:8888 -respout /dev/null 2>&1
